marker.description: A green-headed pin is inserted into the medial surface of the frontal lobe, likely indicating the cingulate gyrus or corpus callosum. A second blue pin is visible near the parietal lobe.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the green pin.
main_explanation: The green pin is located on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere, superior to the corpus callosum. This anatomical position corresponds to the cingulate gyrus, a part of the limbic system.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following structures is located immediately inferior to the structure indicated by the green pin?
supporting_question.explanation: The cingulate gyrus is a band of cortical grey matter that arches over the corpus callosum. Therefore, the corpus callosum is the major structure located immediately inferior to it.
